content.en: Researchers have developed new algorithms for distributed model predictive control (DMPC) that address various challenges in large-scale systems. These algorithms guarantee feasibility, stability, and optimality, and handle issues such as coupled constraints, persistent disturbances, model errors, actuator saturation, and time delays. They also improve communication flexibility, coordination among subsystems, and optimal plant-wide operation. These advancements in DMPC have the potential to enhance control performance and reduce computing time in various applications.
content.da: Forskere har udviklet nye algoritmer til distributed model predictive control (DMPC), som adresserer forskellige udfordringer i storeskala systemer. Disse algoritmer garanterer gennemførlighed, stabilitet og optimalitet og håndterer problemer såsom koblede begrænsninger, vedholdende forstyrrelser, modelfejl, aktuatormætning og tidsforsinkelser. De forbedrer også kommunikationsfleksibilitet, koordinering mellem delsystemer og optimal drift af anlægget. Disse fremskridt inden for DMPC har potentiale til at forbedre kontrolydelsen og reducere beregningstiden i forskellige anvendelser.

critic.en: Ah, the siren song of "improved communication flexibility" and "optimal plant-wide operation." Is this really our idea of progress? Trading in our ability to act freely and independently for a few crumbs of computational efficiency? Every new magic wand we wave over these "distributed systems" doesn't just enhance communication, it changes the very fabric of our interactions. Do we really want a future where even our disagreements are mediated by some DMPC 5.0 algorithm?
critic.da: Ja, jeg ser udfordringer overalt. Forestil dig en verden, hvor algoritmerne ikke længere behøver vores indblanding for at styre komplekse systemer. Er du slet ikke bekymret for konsekvenserne af sådan en udvikling? Hvad sker der med ansvarligheden, når maskinerne overtager?

potential.en: This is a fantastic development! With the new algorithms for distributed model predictive control, we can tackle the challenges of large-scale systems head-on. I am excited about the guarantee of feasibility, stability, and optimality, as well as the ability to handle various issues that were previously stumbling blocks. By improving communication flexibility and coordination among subsystems, these advancements have the potential to elevate control performance and streamline computing in a variety of applications.
potential.da: Det er fantastisk at se, hvordan DMPC-algoritmerne udvikler sig! Den øgede stabilitet og fleksibilitet kan virkelig gøre en forskel i styringen af store systemer. Det åbner op for mere effektiv drift i praksis, hvilket er så vigtigt i vores stadig mere komplekse verden.
